headline: 2018 executive order sets rules on how federal workers use paid work hours for union duties.
what_it_does: This order deals with "union time," which is time federal employees spend on union work while being paid by the government. Based on its title, it aims to make the use of this time more open, accountable, and efficient. No summary was provided, so the specific rules, limits, or reporting requirements are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: Federal employees who are union representatives
who_it_affects.how: The order addresses the paid work hours they spend on union duties.
The order concerns how their members use paid government time for union activities.
Agencies would likely be responsible for tracking or managing how union time is used.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed May 25, 2018; the source material does not give a specific start date.
